rows.behavior: Do nothing unless the executable's PE identity and every function signature match the sheets.
rows.evidence: Live 2026-10-13: on the supported build the log shows 'ready on game 4.630.0.0'; other programs in the game folder that load the file (crash handler, video helper) stay untouched.

rows.behavior: Run the mod's tick once per frame on the game thread; catch faults and turn off after the fault limit.
rows.evidence: Live: tick ran every frame for a 5-minute soak; logged cost 52 microseconds on average, 1.3 ms at worst, zero faults.

rows.behavior: Read the local hero's transform, joints and suit part ids each frame.
rows.evidence: Live: host log lists the worn suit's part ids; poses left the game at 20 per second while in the city and stopped at the main menu and during a checkpoint reload.

rows.behavior: Spawn, activate, dress and remove the other player's double.
rows.evidence: Live: double spawned, was dressed in a suit that was not loaded on this game (Homemade Suit while the player wore the Bodega Cat Suit) with its mask shown, followed a suit change, and came back after a checkpoint reload.

rows.behavior: Place the double and write interpolated joints every frame.
rows.evidence: Live: recorded clip shows the double running, climbing and landing in step with the poses it was sent; Melty test check pose-mirrored passed (written poses stay in place between frames).

rows.behavior: Pack and unpack poses: quantized rotations and positions, changed-joint mask, scaled joints.
rows.evidence: tests/codec_test.cpp passes in every build: round trip within tolerance, dead-band never drifts past its slack, truncated and baseless input refused. Live traffic 40 to 60 KB/s.

rows.behavior: Host on a TCP port or join the address from Melty; hello, suit, pose, away, ping; drop a silent peer.
rows.evidence: Live with two copies of the game on one PC: host listened, second copy connected and exchanged hello, host accepted it again after an 8 s stall. With the echo test peer: suit, pose, away and ping all flowed both ways. Not tested: two PCs over the internet through Melty's relay.

rows.behavior: Read join= at start, empty the log, write the join address, joined and failed lines.
rows.evidence: Live: host wrote 'Melty join address: <host LAN address>:47584'; second copy read join=, emptied the log and wrote 'Melty joined: <host LAN address>:47584'. setup_multiplayer read both logs: joined, matches host.

rows.behavior: In a Melty test run, show a mirrored double through the full codec and report the checks.
rows.evidence: Live dry run with a test file: checks file received pass hosting-open, pass hero-found, pass double-spawned, pass pose-mirrored.

rows.behavior: Load as winmm.dll beside the game and pass every winmm.dll export on to Windows' own copy.
rows.evidence: Live: the game loads the file as winmm.dll at start and plays normally; all 181 winmm exports are forwarded with Windows' own ordinals.

rows.behavior: Show the other player on the minimap: before the double is activated, give its MapElement the person-marker type and the always-show flag.
rows.evidence: Two PCs on one home network, 2026-10-13, build 0.2.0: the creator reported it works; both mod logs show no marker failure; the creator's 74-second Steam clip (media/miles-together-map-marker-2026-10-13.mp4) shows the person marker on the minimap following the other player while swinging. Earlier on one PC with tools/echo_peer.py: shown at 8, 36 and 85 m, removed on disconnect, back on reconnect. The pause map does not show it.

rows.behavior: Shared world state, part 1: both players send their lighting mode (time of day and weather); the joiner switches to the host's when it differs. The world message itself is sent and read in src/net.cpp.
rows.evidence: Two PCs on one home network, 2026-10-14, build 0.3.0: the creator reported it works. Joiner log: 'matching the host's time of day and weather (lighting mode 1; this game had 2)' and later '(lighting mode 2; this game had 1)', each at the moment the host came back from its pause menu after changing the time of day; both games exited with code 0. Earlier on one PC against tools/echo_peer.py --listen: matched modes 0 and 4. Not seen in the logs: the joiner changing its own time of day and being switched back.

rows.behavior: Shared enemies, part 1 (visual): the host finds enemies (objects with a BotHealth component) near either player and sends each one's actor asset, transform and joints; the joiner spawns an inert puppet of the same actor for each and poses it every frame, and removes it when the host says it is gone or goes quiet. Messages are sent and read in src/net.cpp.
rows.evidence: Probe on one PC: an inert firefighter puppet posed every frame from a live firefighter's 135 joints moved naturally. Not yet built. First two-PC test (2026-10-14): the joiner crashed three times while activating rifle-thug puppets (write to an unallocated per-type component list at 0x1E2609F). Joint counts found by scanning for w = 1 were wrong (223, 239, 241 for one actor), so puppets were written past their joint arrays. Fixed: the count now comes from the live enemy's animation controller, and at most one puppet is spawned per frame. Second two-PC test: no crash, but nothing shown: the host's thug actors (melee thug, baton thugs, pistol thug) were not loaded on the joiner. Fixed: the joiner requests an enemy's actor asset when it is missing and spawns the puppet once it has loaded. Third two-PC test: the joiner showed all 11 shared enemies, but the creator saw only some. actor_asset_lookup found a requested actor 1 ms after the request, so the first 9 puppets were spawned from actors still loading; the later ones, spawned a second on, were fine. Fixed: wait asset_settle_time after a request before spawning that actor.

rows.behavior: Adds Go to your friend (only while connected) and Start a crime (test) to the game's pause list. Choosing the first warps you next to the other player; the second makes the random crime system pick a crime now.
rows.evidence: Probes on one PC: added items showed with our labels and their selection reached menu_select; warp_object moved a standing hero 57 m; forcing the crime cooldown picked a crime. Not yet built. Built and tested on one PC with tools/echo_peer.py: Start a crime (test) showed and picked a crime; Go to your friend showed only while connected and moved a perched hero 61 m to the friend (139.5, 7.4, -1986.1 to 181.5, 1, -1941.1) and he stayed, with the warp_action_release byte set. Not yet tested on two PCs.

rows.behavior: One set of crimes: while joined, the joiner's own random crime countdown is held so its game starts none, and its Start a crime (test) asks the host's game to start one instead.
